images.name: Aegidius Strauch II
images.reason: Replace Strauch I church-leadership concept with Strauch II chronology and astronomy.

images.name: Johann Pasch
images.reason: Remove conjunction astronomy as the primary contribution; emphasize attested philological scholarship.

images.name: Johann Andreas Planer
images.reason: Show the attested De nive disputations rather than generic academic office.

images.name: Abu Abdallah al-Natili
images.reason: Add the documented revision of Arabic Dioscorides instead of depicting only Avicenna’s tutor.

images.name: Kamal al-Din Ibn Yunus
images.reason: Make the specific commentary on geometric constructions visible, not generic Mosul scholarship.

images.name: Sharaf al-Din al-Masudi al-Marwazi
images.reason: Represent both critical Avicennian philosophy and Jahan-danish, not astronomy alone.

images.name: Omar Khayyam
images.reason: Make securely attested mathematics and calendar work primary; do not imply certainty for attributed poetry.

images.name: Bonifazius Erasmi
images.reason: Show calendar compilation associated with Cranach’s woodcut rather than only a generic first classroom.

refinement.prompt: Use case: precise-object-edit. Refine this Strauch II chronology-and-astronomy website artwork. Preserve its 16:9 aspect, beautiful painterly realism, historical study, warm/cool lighting and book/armillary/hourglass subject. Remove EVERY letter, numeral, pseudo-letter and inscription from ALL walls, maps, book spines and brass rings: replace writing with clean plain materials or simple non-alphabetic decorative lines. The glaring writing at the upper left must disappear. Recompose ONLY the main still life into a narrower vertical cluster: complete closed chronology book at x=80–93%, complete smaller armillary above at x=81–94%, small hourglass beneath at x=86–94%, all comfortably inside image boundaries. Keep actual room continuing left, no flat empty fill, no portrait, no new objects. Must look gorgeous on a rightmost 24-percent portrait crop, with the full main book recognizable. No text anywhere.

limitations: Editorial illustrations, not historical photographs, facsimiles or evidence of teacher-student relationships.
